intro: There's no single 'best' platform: there's the best fit for your email, budget and appetite for setting things up. Here are the five realistic options, plus two more technical alternatives, compared on the same criteria. Every option has real downsides, and they're listed.
saves: Choosing well up front saves you from rebuilding everything in three months. Choosing badly is recoverable too: your instructions are plain text and move with you.
methodNote: Prices and features change often, sometimes monthly. We checked the vendors' own pages where we could reach them and reputable reviews where we couldn't, and noted where sources disagreed. Always confirm the price at checkout before you subscribe.
fxNote: Several platforms charge in US dollars or euros. Pound figures are approximate, converted at roughly £0.75 to the dollar and £0.86 to the euro, and VAT may be added at checkout.
whatsappNote: Honest news on WhatsApp: none of these options can work inside your personal WhatsApp. Zapier, Make and n8n can connect to the separate WhatsApp Business Platform, but that needs a Meta business setup, a registered business number and recipients who've opted in. For most people the practical answer is: the agent drafts the message, you copy it into WhatsApp and send it yourself. That's also the safest approach under the marketing rules.

platforms.name: Claude
platforms.oneLiner: A writing-strong AI assistant with Projects, connectors to Gmail, Google Drive and Canva, and scheduled tasks that run in the cloud.

cost.label: About £15–18 a month
cost.free: Free plan for trying it out (no scheduled tasks)
cost.note: US$20 a month, or US$17 a month billed yearly (US$200). Billed in dollars; VAT may be added.

platforms.setupText: Low: create a Project, paste instructions, connect Gmail.
platforms.ongoingText: Low: read the drafts, tweak instructions now and then.

gmail.note: Reads, searches and creates drafts. Plan on drafts rather than sending.

outlook.note: The Microsoft 365 connector needs a business Microsoft account. Personal @outlook.com or @hotmail.com addresses can't connect.

whatsapp.note: Writes messages for you to paste.

social.note: Writes posts and captions for you to post.

sheets.note: The Google Drive connector reads your files; editing a spreadsheet directly is more limited.

canva.note: Canva connector available in the connectors directory.

background.text: Good. Since 6 October 2026, new scheduled tasks run in Anthropic's cloud, so your laptop can be closed. They run on a clock (e.g. Mondays 7am), not the moment an email arrives.

platforms.data: US company. On personal plans you choose in Settings → Privacy whether your chats help train models; if you opt out, chats are kept for about 30 days. No UK-only data storage on personal plans.

lockin.text: Instructions are plain text you can copy to any other platform.

platforms.goodIf: you use Gmail, want one tool for writing, research and scheduled briefings, and are happy to copy-paste social posts and WhatsApp messages yourself.
pros: Excellent at writing in a natural British tone
Projects keep each agent briefed with its own instructions and files
Scheduled tasks keep running with your laptop closed
Gmail drafting (not sending) is a built-in safety net
cons: Can't connect a personal Outlook.com or Hotmail inbox
No WhatsApp, Instagram or Facebook connection
Usage limits: on a heavy day you can hit a cap and wait a few hours
Can't react the instant an email arrives; it checks on a schedule
Features get renamed and reorganised often

sources.label: Claude help: Cowork on web, desktop and mobile

platforms.name: ChatGPT
platforms.oneLiner: The best-known AI assistant, with custom GPTs, Projects, agent mode, image creation and scheduled tasks, including tasks triggered by Gmail.

cost.label: About £19–20 a month
cost.free: Free and cheaper 'Go' plans exist, but without Gmail-triggered tasks
cost.note: US$20 list price; UK checkout reported at about £16 + 20% VAT.

platforms.setupText: Low: create a custom GPT or Project, paste instructions, connect Gmail.
platforms.ongoingText: Low: check drafts and scheduled results.

gmail.note: Searches and reads email; Plus can start tasks from Gmail activity. Sending varies, so plan on drafts.

outlook.note: Outlook connector is aimed mainly at business plans; support on personal Plus is limited.

whatsapp.note: Writes messages for you to paste.

social.note: Writes posts and creates images for you to post.

canva.note: Canva app works on Plus with a free Canva account.

background.text: Fair. Scheduled tasks and Gmail-triggered tasks are available on Plus. Some users report runs that can't reach connected apps, so check results at first.

platforms.data: US company. Chats can be used to train models unless you switch off 'Improve the model for everyone' in Settings → Data controls.

lockin.text: Custom GPTs live inside ChatGPT, but you can copy the instructions out.

platforms.goodIf: you already use ChatGPT, use Gmail, and want tasks that start when an enquiry email arrives, or an assistant you can share with your team.
pros: Familiar, with endless tutorials and YouTube help
Custom GPTs are easy to share with team members (great for a recruit FAQ)
Gmail-triggered tasks on Plus
Built-in image creation for social posts
cons: Model training on your chats is on by default; switch it off
Limited support for personal Outlook.com
No WhatsApp, Instagram or Facebook connection
Plans, features and names change frequently
Usage caps on the most capable models

platforms.name: Microsoft Copilot
platforms.oneLiner: Copilot built into Word, Excel and Outlook on a personal Microsoft 365 subscription. Helpful for writing, but not really an agent platform.

cost.label: About £8.49 a month
cost.free: Free Copilot app with basic features
cost.note: £8.49/month or £84.99/year as reported by Which? (July 2025); not re-confirmed. Includes Office apps and storage. Copilot use is limited by monthly AI credits.

platforms.setupText: Very low if you already have Microsoft 365.
platforms.ongoingText: Medium: no schedules, so you start every job yourself.

gmail.note: Copilot features are built around Outlook.com accounts.

outlook.note: Built into Outlook for personal accounts.

sheets.note: Works in Excel, not Google Sheets.

background.text: Poor. No scheduled or background agents on personal plans: you prompt it each time. Proper agent-building (Copilot Studio) is priced for businesses.

platforms.data: Microsoft personal account. The real risk is mixing it up with your NHS Microsoft account, which may also have Copilot.

lockin.text: Your documents stay yours; prompts are easy to copy elsewhere.

platforms.goodIf: you already pay for Microsoft 365 Personal and mainly want writing help in Word and Outlook. Use it alongside a proper agent platform, not instead of one.
pros: You may already be paying for it
Works inside Word, Excel and Outlook
Familiar interface
cons: Very easy to confuse with your NHS work account. A serious risk for you
Limited monthly AI credits on personal plans
No scheduled tasks or background agents
Real agent-building tools are priced for businesses
platforms.warning: Never use your NHS Microsoft account, work device or NHS Copilot for the business.

sources.label: Licensing School: Copilot in Personal and Family

platforms.name: Zapier
platforms.oneLiner: The best-known automation tool. It connects thousands of apps and now includes AI Agents that can make decisions along the way.

cost.label: Free to start; about £15–60 a month as you grow
cost.free: Free plan for simple Zaps; Agents free for 400 activities a month
cost.note: Professional Zaps about US$20–30 a month; Agents Pro US$50 a month (or about US$33 billed yearly). Agents are metered separately in 'activities'.

platforms.setupText: Higher: you build step-by-step workflows and test them.
platforms.ongoingText: Low once working; check now and then that nothing has broken.

whatsapp.note: WhatsApp Business Platform only: needs Meta Business Manager, a registered business number and a paid Zapier plan.

social.note: Facebook Pages and Instagram Business accounts (e.g. posting, lead forms), not personal DMs.

canva.note: Check the specific action you need.

background.text: Excellent. Built to run all the time and react the moment something arrives.

platforms.data: US company; your data passes through Zapier for each step. Check its data processing terms before connecting client data.

lockin.text: Workflows and agents would need rebuilding by hand elsewhere.

platforms.goodIf: you want things to happen automatically the moment something arrives, or need to join up lots of apps, including Outlook.com.
pros: Connects to more apps than anything else, including Outlook.com
Reacts instantly to new emails, forms and spreadsheet rows
Free tier to experiment with
Mix fixed workflows with AI steps
cons: Costs climb as you use more, and 'activities' are hard to predict
Feels like building, not chatting, so there's more to learn
WhatsApp setup via Meta is genuinely fiddly
Writing quality depends on your instructions and settings

sources.label: 5minsystems: Zapier Agents pricing for small business
Katteb: Zapier price and agents add-on

platforms.name: Lindy
platforms.oneLiner: A dedicated 'AI assistant' builder, designed for hands-off agents that handle your inbox, meetings and follow-ups.

cost.label: About £23–38 a month
cost.note: Sources in 2026 disagree: US$29.99 (newer) or US$49.99 (older) for the entry plan, with monthly credits.

platforms.setupText: Medium: templates help, but there are lots of settings.
platforms.ongoingText: Medium: keep an eye on credit use.

sheets.note: Lindy claims 1,000+ integrations; check the one you need.

background.text: Good: runs on triggers and schedules. When monthly credits run out, agents pause unless you buy top-ups.

platforms.data: US company. Reports on its UK/EU GDPR status conflict. Ask for its data processing agreement before using client data.

lockin.text: Agents are built in Lindy's own format.

platforms.goodIf: you want a hands-off inbox assistant, don't mind a smaller company and will keep an eye on credits.
pros: Designed for hands-off assistants
Ready-made templates for email and follow-ups
Works with Gmail and Outlook
cons: Prices changed during 2026 and sources disagree
Reviewers report credits running out quickly
Customer reviews complain about support
Smaller company: more risk of big changes or closure
No free plan

platforms.name: Make
platforms.oneLiner: A visual automation tool: you draw your workflow as a map of connected bubbles. Cheaper than Zapier, with AI Agents in beta.

cost.label: Free tier; paid from about £7–9 a month
cost.free: Free plan with 1,000 credits a month
cost.note: Core about US$9–12 a month depending on billing. AI steps use extra credits. Sources disagree slightly.

platforms.setupText: Higher: powerful, but a real learning curve.
platforms.ongoingText: Medium: workflows sometimes need fixing when apps change.

background.text: Excellent: built to run all the time.

platforms.data: European company with an EU data region option. Check which region your account uses.
platforms.goodIf: you enjoy tinkering and want the cheapest always-on automation.
pros: Cheapest paid automation
Visual map makes workflows easy to see
EU data region option
cons: Steeper learning curve than Zapier
AI Agents still in beta; pricing may change
Credit maths can be confusing

platforms.name: n8n
platforms.oneLiner: A powerful, open-source automation tool favoured by techies. Its cloud version is hosted in the EU.

cost.label: About £17–21 a month
cost.note: €20 a month billed yearly or €24 monthly for 2,500 runs.

background.text: Excellent: built to run all the time.

platforms.data: Cloud version hosted in the EU (Frankfurt). Open source, so you can export everything.

lockin.text: Open source; workflows export as files.

platforms.goodIf: you have a techy friend to help and want maximum control with EU hosting. Honestly, too technical as a first step.
pros: EU hosting
Very flexible
Low lock-in
cons: Built for technical users
Hardest to set up and fix
Run limits on the starter plan

emailHelp.title: Not sure which email you use for the business?
points: Ends in @outlook.com, @hotmail.com or @live.com: that's a personal Microsoft account.
Uses your own name, like hello@yourtravel.co.uk: ask whoever set it up whether it runs on Google Workspace or Microsoft 365.
Ends in nhs.net or nhs.uk: stop. That's your work email and must never be used for the business.
emailHelp.advice: If you don't yet have a separate business email, set one up before choosing a platform. A free Gmail address is the most widely supported by every option here. Your host agency may also provide one.
